idiom_name: urllib3.util.Retry (idempotent-method allow-list) or tenacity + stable Idempotency-Key
implementation_notes: urllib3 and requests make the safe default explicit: Retry.allowed_methods defaults to DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and TRACE, so a POST is never retried unless the caller opts in - and the moment you opt in, the server is owed a stable key (uuid.uuid4() minted before the call and stored with the pending work). Where the retry must depend on business logic, tenacity's @retry decorator wraps a function that closes over that key; the decorator replaces the hand-written loop, while the key and the receiver-side record stay where they were. urllib3 documents that read errors are raised after the request was sent and 'may have side-effects', which is exactly the case the pattern exists for.
pitfalls: allowed_methods is a security-relevant default: adding "POST" without a key turns every read timeout into a second attempt at a side effect, whereas retrying connection errors is safe either way.
The key must live outside the decorated function - a uuid.uuid4() inside charge() is a new logical operation on every attempt.
Sharing one Session/PoolManager keeps connection reuse; building a fresh Session per retry both loses pooling and makes it easy to forget the request-level key assignment.
